subject: health
title: Mastery check: community health helpers and access
essentialQuestion: How do I make a sound decision, set a goal I can reach, and advocate for health beyond myself?
materials: two or more adult-approved health sources for comparison
paper or a digital tool for a goal plan and advocacy piece
keyPoints: Community health includes clinics, school nurses, pharmacists, dentists, libraries, and food programmes.
Access is not equal: cost, transport, language, and disability all get in the way.
Knowing what exists locally is itself a health skill.
Helping someone reach a service is a genuine form of advocacy.
privacySafeScenario: A family new to the area does not know where to get a child's vaccination. Who could help, and how would you find out?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about community health helpers and access to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Explain community health helpers and access to someone who has not learned it yet, using one example.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about community health helpers and access.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Goal tracking may be a checklist, a spoken check-in, a drawing, or an adult-recorded note. The advocacy piece may be a poster, letter, slide, spoken message, or described plan. No public posting, publication, or performance is required.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about community health helpers and access under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, pick one household health habit worth improving and talk about what would make it stick. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
